assignments.evidence: Funerary blessing pair 'xby kpt hquqptntw / xb kpt hquqvantw': xby stands parallel to glossary xb (bread), the classic water/bread pair (123 tokens).
Follows both xby (water) and xb (bread) in every blessing ('xby kpt ... xb kpt ...'), so it is the quantity word.
Title before NAME in genealogies and seals; in the royal stela the series 'gyatmsq xnqeqjj hgamsq htwbymsq' gives ruler / [named person] / hga / viceroy.
'ryu knjq fp' and its variant 'ryu kn jq fp': kn is the first part of knjq (goddess) = kn + njq (woman); it also occurs alone in royal texts.
Livestock count 'vfoq 3 jqkt 4 ntfr ...': it comes after vfoq (bull) with its own number.
Captive lists 'xoa 32 njq 135', 'xoa 100 njq 100', 'xoa 58 njq 223', and 'njq w fr xoa w fr': it always pairs with njq.
It is inside njqbt (sister) and knjq (goddess = god + woman), and it pairs with xoa in the counts of captives.
Predicate 'kfyfyrq' ('is good') ends texts; 'xby kfy ... xb kfy' (good water / good bread); 'gyat kfy fy kn f r kfy fy' (good ruler, good god).
Epithet after a noun: 'ryu knjq fp' (Isis, great goddess), 'btktsnjq fp', 'gy vovt fp NAME'.
Kin term in genealogies: 'NAME wkfyrq' (wife) ... 'NAME ubtfyrq' (mother); also 'ubt fq gyat wk fy' (mother of ..., wife of the ruler).
'xeb keh w fq' / 'xeb key' (xeb of xkeh = Amun); a temple title listed beside hga and htwby in the royal stela.
Variant of btaqnt, the father-filiation verb in 'NAME btaqntfyrq' (paired with bjvt, born of); 'kbt htfkyu xbyfqb staqnt fy' = child begotten by the general.
'hga NAME NAME boy' (two princes); 'jqfpf boy ryu hqfgtbtf ryu btortbtf' introduces two Isis forms (of place A and of place B).
'xa kbt' (xa + child); plural xawt closes the captive series 'xoawt f ... njqwt f ... xawt fq' (men, women, boys).
The royal epithet 'gyat ... keqbnt knfto' is xkeq/keq (Amun) + bnt: 'beloved of Amun ... of the gods'.
A counted noun in booty and royal texts: 'fr xwa xvqjtov rq 1626', '... 1032', 'xwa jto 5000', next to captive and bull counts.
Verb with -nt (like the blessing verbs 'hquqpt-nt-w'): 'btrqwbq xat nt NAME stuyx' asks for the adoration to be received; the same root xa- appears in the war stela 'xaovbtnt' of seized captives.
'gyat bat' (the ruler offers); 'bato' and 'batbyv kfyfy' (the offering is good) in adoration texts; title 'kftntsyw batst' beside 'kftntsyw xbyst' (of water).
